title: Zombie type
description: A zombie type, per docs/14-zombies.md. Adding one is a JSON entry with zero code, provided every behavior tag it references already exists.

id.description: Stable namespaced id. Permanent once shipped.

extends.description: Id of another zombie type to inherit from.

introducedInWave.description: Mutation wave that introduces this type. 0 is present from the start.

sensory.description: Channel weights. docs/14-zombies.md#sensory-profiles: there is no single silence.

locomotion.description: How fast this type moves, in each of the states it has. `speed` is a multiplier on a human walk; the rest are fractions of this type's own `speed`, so a faster type is faster in every state without four numbers to keep in agreement. docs/29-movement-and-stances.md: a zombie's speeds are fields in its JSON entry rather than constants in a module.

speed.description: Purposeful movement -- closing on a stimulus. A multiplier on a human walk, so 0.8 is slower than you walk whatever the pace is set to, which is what makes retreat a real option.

wander.description: Aimless drift, as a fraction of `speed`. Idle bodies barely move.

mill.description: Investigating on arrival, as a fraction of `speed`. Slower than drifting.

crawl.description: What is left once locomotion is destroyed, as a fraction of `speed`. docs/14-zombies.md#damage-model: a zombie with a destroyed pelvis crawls, is quiet, and is still perfectly capable of biting an ankle.

body.description: Health by body part. Meaningful damage is to the head or to locomotion.

spread.description: Persistent per-individual angular bias on gradient ascent, in radians. Without it they form conga lines rather than a horde -- docs/14-zombies.md#gradient-ascent-is-not-sufficient-on-its-own.

behaviors.description: Behavior tags. Every one must be implemented, or load fails.

alarm.description: Screamer-style relay. docs/14: converts a small mistake into a regional event.

appearance.description: What this looks like. docs/20: adding a type is a JSON entry with zero code, and appearance was the last axis where that was untrue -- presentation used to pick colours by type id in the draw loop. Omit it entirely and the renderer falls back to its role colours, which is the normal state until art exists.

sprite.description: Registry key, resolved to assets/sprites/<key>.png by presentation/appearance.gd. A key, not a path, so content stays engine-agnostic. A key naming a file that does not exist fails the appearance gate rather than silently drawing nothing.

tint.description: Colour for the procedural fallback, and a modulate over the sprite when one exists.
